title: Celestica at SC26: From Open Architecture to Rack-Scale Operational Advantage
summary: Discover Celestica at SC26 (Booth #4634). Explore our open AI infrastructure, 1.6T networking, high-performance storage, and rack-scale integration solutions.
body_markdown:
WRITTEN BY


Matt Roman,


Senior Director of Product Line Management


share


- LinkedIn


2026-11-12


SC26 brings together the HPC community under the banner of “HPC Unites,” highlighting collaboration to advance research and explore how high-performance computing empowers global communities.


Celestica is bringing that same collaborative ethos to AI infrastructure—converging open networking, storage, compute, rack-scale design and engineering, manufacturing at scale, software and services, and a partner ecosystem to help customers move with confidence from initial design to scaled production and operational advantage.


AI infrastructure is frequently discussed as a checklist of isolated parts: accelerators, switches, storage arrays, power shelves, and cooling loops. But AI infrastructure builders do not deploy a parts list. They deploy tightly coupled systems that must sustain massive data throughput, maximize GPU utilization, and adapt as models, silicon generations, and thermal profiles evolve.


The primary challenge is rarely selecting a single component; it is orchestrating compute, storage, and networking fabric around the workload—bridging the gap between an architectural blueprint and production-ready capacity with absolute confidence. At its core, Celestica’s focus is turning open architecture into an enduring AI operational advantage for our customers.


## Preserving Choice, Backed by System-Level Engineering


Open networking, storage, and compute preserve strategic agility, freeing Celestica customers from vendor lock-in as they expand. Yet choice without deep systems engineering creates operational friction.


Celestica pairs open hardware and software with integration expertise honed while building some of the largest AI fabrics in the world. We combine open platforms and software with comprehensive[rack integration services](https://www.celestica.com/our-expertise/platform-solutions/rack-integration-services) and[IT asset intelligence](https://cls.celestica.com/our-expertise/services/it-asset-management) —[designing](https://www.celestica.com/our-expertise/services/design-and-engineering) , integrating, validating, and supporting architectures built specifically to manage the extreme thermal and power densities of modern AI clusters.


## Start with the Workload, Not the Port Speed


Networking demands vary significantly across back-end scale-out fabrics, front-end fabrics, scale-up fabrics, and management fabrics. Celestica’s open rack-scale data center network[switching portfolio](https://www.celestica.com/our-expertise/platform-solutions/networking) addresses each tier of the network fabric and is purpose-built to support the most demanding AI/ML and HPC requirements. These fabric tiers serve different workload needs, from connecting GPUs across a cluster to linking users and managing the network itself.


Complementing the network, Celestica Services brings rack integration and advanced liquid cooling capabilities to help manage the thermal and power demands of AI infrastructure.


- **Back-end Scale-Out Fabric:** Scaling the AI cluster from 800G to 1.6T can be accomplished by deploying Celestica DS5000 and DS6000 series data center switches, including the[DS5000](https://cls.celestica.com/hardware-platforms/ds5000/) ,[DS5001](https://cls.celestica.com/hardware-platforms/ds5001/) ,[DS6000](https://cls.celestica.com/hardware-platforms/ds6000/) ,[DS6001](https://cls.celestica.com/hardware-platforms/ds6001/) and[DS6005](https://cls.celestica.com/hardware-platforms/ds6005/) . These purpose-built data center switches are essential building blocks when deploying massive RoCEv2 fabrics.
- **Back-End Scale-up Fabric:** Unifying across traditional boundaries to connect multiple AI servers and racks inside the AI data center can be accomplished with Celestica’s next-generation DS6000 series of 102.4Tb switches. Optimized for ultra-low-latency to support scale-up topologies, the[DS6010](https://cls.celestica.com/hardware-platforms/ds6010/) which is a data center switch qualified for[AMD’s Helios rack-scale AI architecture](https://www.celestica.com/blog/article/accelerating-the-next-era-of-ai-celestica-and-amd-collaborate-on-the-amd-helios-rackscale-solution) , the[DS6000](https://cls.celestica.com/hardware-platforms/ds6000/) ,[DS6001](https://cls.celestica.com/hardware-platforms/ds6001/) , and the[DS6005](https://cls.celestica.com/hardware-platforms/ds6005/) , are all excellent choices for scale-up fabrics.
- **Front-End Fabric:** Connecting users, data, and applications requires a power-optimized data center switch that can bridge 400G compute nodes straight to 800G fabrics. Celestica[DS4150](https://cls.celestica.com/hardware-platforms/ds4150/) ,[DS5001](https://cls.celestica.com/hardware-platforms/ds5001/) , and[DS5000](https://cls.celestica.com/hardware-platforms/ds5000/) data center switches are an excellent choice for this place in the data center network.
- **Management Fabric:** Operating this open fabric with confidence requires visibility, orchestration, control, telemetry and lifecycle management, all of which depend on a scalable, power-optimized top-of-rack management switch. This is the perfect job for the[ES1010](https://cls.celestica.com/hardware-platforms/es1010es1050/) and the[DS2010](https://cls.celestica.com/hardware-platforms/ds2010/) .


[The Celestica Networking Portfolio](https://www.celestica.com/our-expertise/platform-solutions/networking) gives AI model builders the flexibility to map the network directly to workload requirements and cluster topology. Dell'Oro Group underscored that execution by recognizing Celestica as the[market-share leader in AI back-end Ethernet network switch sales for Q1 and Q2 2026](https://www.delloro.com/newsroom/ai-back-end-networks-switch-sales-surpass-front-end-networks-for-the-first-time-in-2q2026/) .


As an OCP Platinum Member, Celestica’s[contributions](https://www.opencompute.org/?s=celestica&_gl=1*2fd9ii*_up*MQ..*_ga*MTI3MjI5NDE5Mi4xNzkzODIxNjQw*_ga_HYNL8C0MSS*czE3OTM4MjE2NDAkbzEkZzAkdDE3OTM4MjE2NDAkajYwJGwwJGgw) extend well beyond hardware exhibits. Our OCP-accepted and OCP-inspired contributions include the DS5000 and[standardized reference architectures](https://www.opencompute.org/documents/open-cluster-designs-aligned-ai-inference-fabric-reference-architecture-pdf/) for AI training (co-authored with technology partner Hedgehog) and AI inference through the[Open Cluster Designs for AI initiative](https://www.opencompute.org/projects/strategic-initiatives/cluster-designs-for-ai/) , among others. Celestica was among the industry partners contributing to the[Open Switch Platform Architecture (OSPA)](https://www.opencompute.org/news/introducing-ospa-unifying-the-switch-platform-layer-for-open-networking/) specification from its launch and is actively tracking the specification; we will accommodate its requirements in relevant platforms. The[initial OSPA 1.0.0 specification](https://github.com/opencomputeproject/OCP-switch-platform-architecture/blob/main/spec/main/OCP_OSPA_Spec.md) is now available.


Storage and compute are equal partners in this open fabric. The[Celestica Storage Portfolio](https://www.celestica.com/our-expertise/platform-solutions/storage) empowers organizations to deploy advanced, cloud-ready data storage architectures and includes:


- **Storage Control:** The next-generation[SC6100](https://cls.celestica.com/hardware-platforms/sc6100/?utm_source=referral_blogsc6100&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=fms2024) and[SC6110](https://cls.celestica.com/hardware-platforms/sc6110/) storage controllers deliver extreme performance and high availability for the most demanding enterprise application workloads, powered by two AMD EPYC™ high-performance microprocessors.
- **Storage Expansion:** To address data growth challenges in enterprise and hyperscale data centers,[SD6300](https://cls.celestica.com/hardware-platforms/sd6300/?utm_source=digital&utm_medium=blog&utm_campaign=sd6300launch) ultra-dense, SAS-4 storage expansion system is a good match for rapid AI data expansion.


[The Celestica Storage Portfolio](https://www.celestica.com/our-expertise/platform-solutions/storage) , integrated alongside open protocols and technologies—such as NVMe-oF, RoCEv2/RDMA, Xinnor xiRAID, and GPUDirect Storage—balances I/O pipelines to keep accelerators saturated.


[Celestica Services](https://www.celestica.com/our-expertise/services/overview) combines global logistics and deployment with maintenance and lifecycle support, helping customers move critical infrastructure into operation and keep it running. Rather than a fixed, one-size-fits-all package, customers can draw on the services that fit their environment, while Celestica validates the system around their specific workloads, with high-density cooling and power delivery designed from day one.


## Converting Openness into Operational Confidence


Open hardware preserves flexibility, but production teams still require carrier-grade software, validated telemetry, and single-source accountability.[SONiCⓇ Distribution by Celestica](https://cls.celestica.com/software/celestica-sonic/) delivers that operational foundation: pre-integrated software, rigorous system-level qualification, and end-to-end enterprise support. It removes the burden of maintaining a bespoke operating stack without compromising the freedom of open networking.


Hardware and software are further backed by Celestica’s global manufacturing footprint, joint design engineering, rack-level integration, and lifecycle services. The result is a unified path that cuts procurement friction, accelerates time-to-first-token, and reduces long-term operational risk.


Figure 1: Celestica AI data center open fabric building blocks for rack-scale operational advantage


## Production Proof at Scale: AI Networking, Enterprise Modernization, and HPC Storage


From sustained AI-fabric workloads and enterprise network modernization to HPC storage, these examples show how Celestica platforms, software, and technology partners work together in real operating environments. Celestica Services adds deployment and lifecycle support across the broader portfolio.


- AI Cloud Deployment at FarmGPU:[FarmGPU](https://www.celestica.com/uploadedFiles/Site/our-expertise/platform-solutions/case-studies/Celestica_and_FarmGPU_Case_Study_2026_11_2.pdf) deployed an 800G AI fabric built on Celestica DS5000 switches and SONiC, demonstrating production stability, wire-speed RoCEv2 throughput, and automated fabric management under sustained loads.
- Network Modernization at a Fortune 100 Retailer: The[case study](https://www.celestica.com/uploadedFiles/Site/our-expertise/platform-solutions/case-studies/Celestica_Retailer_Customer_Case_Study_9_1_2026.pdf) describes how the retailer modernized thousands of network devices with Celestica open switches, third party orchestration, and SONiC—creating a scalable, vendor-neutral network and reporting a 50% reduction in network expenditure.
- Top-Tier HPC Storage Performance: At[Helma](https://www.celestica.com/blog/article/powering-germanys-most-powerful-university-ai-supercomputer-celesticas-role-in-the-helma-project) , Celestica SC6100 controllers with Xinnor xiRAID and Lustre power a half-rack, all-NVMe file system that ranked third globally in IO500 and first among Lustre-based systems.


#### **Built for Adaptability and Scale**


AI infrastructure will continue to see rapid churn across silicon architectures, power envelopes, and cluster topologies. A resilient deployment model allows operators to modernize without rebuilding their operational framework from scratch. By uniting high-performance compute, storage, switching, and rack-scale integration under open standards, Celestica gives AI builders the agility to deploy mission-critical capacity faster, minimize deployment risk, and scale sustainably.


## Connect with Celestica at SC26


Join us at **Booth #4634** to see rack-scale open architecture in action:


-


**Storage Systems:** The SD6300 high-density expansion system and the SC6100 PCIe Gen5 all-flash controller will be on display.


-


**Next-Gen Networking:** The DS6000 family (including the DS6001, the new DS6005, and DS6010), the DS4150, an integrated virtual rack display, and a feature demonstration of SONiCⓇ Distribution by Celestica


-


**SCinet Collaboration:** Celestica has contributed a DS5000 800G switch and high-speed optics to help interconnect[SCinet’s Network Research Exhibits](https://sc26.supercomputing.org/scinet/) , powering active workloads. (Architecture details will be highlighted on-site).


Schedule time with our technical leadership through the[Celestica SC26 portal](https://cls.celestica.com/events/sc26/?utm_source=cblog&utm_medium=website&utm_campaign=sc26) , or visit us on the showroom floor to discuss your cluster architecture.

AUTHOR BIO


Matt Roman


Senior Director of Product Line Management


Matt is the Senior Director of Product Line Management in Celestica’s Platform Solutions group, where he drives technical marketing, go-to-market strategy, and software ecosystem partnerships. A 25+ year IT industry veteran, he brings deep expertise across AI, cloud, enterprise, and telecom sectors. Prior to Celestica, Matt held senior product management and marketing leadership roles at Edgecore Networks, Extreme Networks, and Enablence Technologies.
